common.rawDenied: raw://** is always denied to visitors regardless of this list

codes.intro: Each code gates a slice of your wiki for a known recipient — a hiring loop, an investor intro, or a single press call. Multiple people can share one code; when someone enters it, the AI asks who they are and assigns them to the code's member list. Each card carries a QR.

codeCorpus.loadError: Couldn’t load this code’s corpus scope. Reload and retry.
codeCorpus.publishedSlice: (whatever you have published — this role keeps no list of its own)
codeCorpus.help: The URIs this code takes back from what the role granted, one per line. It can only subtract, never add — whatever you write here will never open what the role didn't grant. Typical use: the role grants subjectivity://** (every opinion), and this code takes back subjectivity://cv (the résumé stays out). Changes only affect sessions issued from now on (the role is frozen when the code is issued).

members.none: no visitor has used this code yet.

conversations.privateHits: {count, plural, one {# session} other {# sessions}} hit private topics
conversations.empty: No conversations yet. Once visitors chat through a code or BYOAI session, you'll see them here.

transcript.groundingTitle: standpoint notes that shaped these answers · not shown to the visitor

prompts.intro: Library of personas. Owner-scoped, no categories. Each one is a piece of writing — the agent becomes whoever you tell it to be here. Used by roles.
prompts.empty: No prompts yet — public is normally seeded on owner claim.

requests.deliveryHint: No verified outbound channel — set one up under Connectors so approving a request can issue a code and send it. Until then you can only mark requests replied/closed by hand.
requests.intro: Submissions from the gate's “no code” path. Mark replied once you've issued a code or written back; close to archive. Owner reads every one personally — that's the point.

roles.intro: A role bundles a prompt (persona), a positive list of corpus URIs the agent can read, a set of skills, and which MCP servers it may call. Codes don’t carry permissions directly — every code assumes a role at issue time and that snapshot is frozen for that session. Edit a role and only future sessions feel it.
roles.empty: No roles yet — public is normally seeded on owner claim.

roleGas.help: Meter this role against its provider's tank. Off (the default) means no usage check runs at all; on means a visitor is stopped once that provider's tank is empty. A provider with no fuel in it is never metered either way.

roleCorpus.help: The positive list of corpus URIs the agent can read, one per line. Match-any: hitting any one line is enough to read, so the grain can be as fine as you like — wiki://thinking/** grants the whole subtree, subjectivity://standpoint grants that one note only. An empty list = nothing at all. Changes only affect sessions issued from now on (the role is frozen when the code is issued).
roleCorpus.publicIsPublished: Whatever you have published — no separate list. This is the identity a visitor gets with no code (and with BYOAI), and it reads an entry only if that entry's own published switch is on. Turn one on from the entry's card under wiki or outputs; there is nothing to edit here, so the two can never say different things.

roleTools.help: What this role may call: your skills, and the external MCP servers you registered under api · mcp. Nothing is granted by default — a server you added is reachable only by the roles you tick it on here. Changes only affect sessions issued from now on (the role is frozen when the code is issued).

roleDock.label: dock
roleDock.help: Trigger phrase — the line the system sends on the visitor's behalf when this button is pressed; the AI handles it as a question from the visitor. For example “summarize the conversation so far”: pressing the button is the same as the visitor typing that line.

roleGhost.label: ghost rule
roleGhost.help: When on, the AI may only steer visitors toward waypoints that cite corpus evidence — empty-evidence steering prompts are dropped (booking and other terminal waypoints are unaffected). Frozen into each session; an access code can override this.

roleDesc.label: about
roleDesc.help: A short line describing this role — who the visitor is and how the AI should treat them. Shown here only (owner-facing).

roleWaypoints.label: waypoints
roleWaypoints.help: Destinations the AI may gently steer visitors toward — one per goal (e.g. “book a call”, “read the cybernetics note”). Each carries a weight (higher = preferred) and, optionally, the corpus evidence that backs it. Mark booking/contact goals as terminal. Frozen into each session; empty = the AI never steers.
